title: DIS dissector: Review support for EntityStateUpdate PDU
description:
Please view issue #20273 

I've fixed the following:
1- entityKind and entityDomain were static variables. They were set in a function named dissect_DIS_FIELDS_ENTITY_TYPE. The problem is this function is called twice, meaning the entityKind and entityDomain were keeping the values set from the second call. I've removed the static variables and handled the Apperance based on the "Entity Type" only.

2- The EntityStateUpdate PDU also relies on these to variables being set beforehand which is a major problem. The ESUPDU relies of the EntityID field to know which object is being updated. Based on that EntityID, the parser shall find the last received EntityStatePDU message, for that given EntityID, to find the object type. In order to resolve that issue, the EntityIdentifier are now stored in a hash map. If the proper EntityIdentifier is not found, an expert warning is shown.

notes.body: Instead of using a `GHashTable` and doing your own memory management, use `wmem_map_t` with  [`wmem_map_new_autoreset()`](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/fb2ef6320a9f55d19074cf081fded96e5d543809/wsutil/wmem/wmem_map.h#L62) in the registration function (which see for details). That would remove the need for the `free_packet_context()` and `proto_cleanup_dis()` functions.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18384/diffs?diff_id=1207681214&start_sha=fe512790402736fb1eb690533bddc641fcee4a07#2b7d2635dd19731ff61759a7b739e76184921e64_36_36)

Wireshark has its own memory management facility, called `wmem`, to do most of that work for you.

```suggestion:-0+0
    packet_context_map = wmem_map_new_autoreset(wmem_epan_scope(), wmem_file_scope(), g_int_hash, g_int_equal);
```

or, if you chose the `GUINT_TO_POINTER()` versions I suggested:

```suggestion:-0+0
    packet_context_map = wmem_map_new_autoreset(wmem_epan_scope(), wmem_file_scope(), g_direct_hash, g_direct_equal);
```

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18384/diffs?diff_id=1207681214&start_sha=fe512790402736fb1eb690533bddc641fcee4a07#2b7d2635dd19731ff61759a7b739e76184921e64_20718_20713)

```suggestion:-0+0
        context = wmem_new0(wmem_file_scope(), packet_context_t);
```

In combination with the `wmem_map_t`, this will let Wireshark handle memory management for you.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18384/diffs?diff_id=1207681214&start_sha=fe512790402736fb1eb690533bddc641fcee4a07#2b7d2635dd19731ff61759a7b739e76184921e64_18073_18071)

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18384/diffs?diff_id=1207681214&start_sha=fe512790402736fb1eb690533bddc641fcee4a07#2b7d2635dd19731ff61759a7b739e76184921e64_18070_18068)

```suggestion:-0+0
        wmem_map_insert(packet_context_map, key, context);
```

or

```suggestion:-0+0
        wmem_map_insert(packet_context_map, GUINT_TO_POINTER(entityid), context);
```

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18384/diffs?diff_id=1207681214&start_sha=fe512790402736fb1eb690533bddc641fcee4a07#2b7d2635dd19731ff61759a7b739e76184921e64_18077_18075)

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18384/diffs?diff_id=1207681214&start_sha=fe512790402736fb1eb690533bddc641fcee4a07#2b7d2635dd19731ff61759a7b739e76184921e64_18322_18318)

```suggestion:-0+0
#include <wireshark.h>
```

This header will always provide a minimal set of functions required for dissectors and other code, including `glib.h` (and compatibility functions to smooth out differences between GLib versions).

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18384/diffs?diff_id=1207681214&start_sha=fe512790402736fb1eb690533bddc641fcee4a07#2b7d2635dd19731ff61759a7b739e76184921e64_22_22)

Thank you for identifying this issue, and for providing a fix for it! On the whole your approach is sound. All the feedback I have is related to memory management; Wireshark has libraries to efficiently handle that for you, so there's no need to manually track and free your own allocations.
